title: The fight over the Siang dam
dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. Four villagers are held under an anti-terror law, a bandh on 23 October ended in tear gas and arson, and on 24 October Pasighat came under prohibitory orders as the chief minister offered talks.

story.text: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is an 11,000 MW hydropower plant being developed by NHPC. Mongabay India reports it would submerge 27 villages, including Yingkiong, Upper Siang's district headquarters, and residents of Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts have consistently opposed it.

The current protests oppose a pre-feasibility study by NHPC at the proposed dam sites, one of the last studies before the dam's detailed project report. Early this month protests turned violent: protesters set fire to vehicles and stormed an MLA's house, and police allegedly lathi-charged protesters on 4 October.

On 9 October four villagers of Geku, Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014; their lawyer says the families at first received only notices. On 11 October the district banned gatherings of five or more people, and on 14 October a sessions court gave 13 people named in two police cases interim protection from arrest.

On 22 October opponents began a 24-hour sit-in at Miracle Ground in Pasighat, demanding an end to survey work, the release of those held and the withdrawal of central armed police. The district allowed it but barred any march beyond the ground. Five more activists were reportedly taken into custody in Pasighat; associates said they did not know where they were held.

On 23 October a 12-hour bandh was called across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang. At Dite-Dime near Geku, police fired tear gas and four to five women were hospitalised; a cameraman was reportedly hit by a shell. That night protesters reportedly set fire to an NHPC office, a police station and police vehicles in Pasighat, and vandalised the homes of local political leaders. The unrest continued until about 4am on 24 October. Protesters want 10 arrested activists freed and an independent inquiry into the police action.

On 24 October shops in Pasighat stayed shut. Police detained five youths for questioning over the vandalism of homes, and from 5pm gatherings of more than five people were barred in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin. Arunachal Times reports five police personnel and several protesters were injured in the clashes. Activists and lawyers, among them human rights lawyer Ebo Mili, surrendered to police, saying the bandh had been peaceful and young people were not behind the violence.

official.text: The detention orders cite a tense and volatile situation, violence and arson, and say they protect public safety. Police say protesters at Dite-Dime threw stones, tried to breach barricades and defied prohibitory orders; the police inspector-general says a case will be registered over the Pasighat violence. Chief Minister Pema Khandu called the incidents regrettable and offered talks: "The government's doors are always open." The state says the dam is mainly meant to store water in view of China's planned dam upstream.

On 9 October four Geku villagers were detained under the state's anti-terror law, and gatherings were banned. On 22 October opponents held a 24-hour sit-in in Pasighat; five more activists were reportedly taken into custody.

On 23 October police fired tear gas during a bandh and four to five women were hospitalised. That night an NHPC office, a police station and vehicles in Pasighat were reportedly set on fire. Protesters want 10 arrested activists freed. On 24 October five youths were detained, gatherings were barred in Pasighat, and lawyer Ebo Mili and other activists surrendered to police.

Official position: the detention orders cite violence and public safety; police say protesters threw stones and defied orders; the chief minister says the government's doors are always open; the state says the dam is meant to store water in view of China's planned dam upstream.

seo_title: Siang dam protests, Arunachal: detentions, bandh and talks offer

whats_new.text: On 24 October police detained five youths over the Pasighat vandalism and barred gatherings of more than five people; activists including lawyer Ebo Mili surrendered, saying the bandh was peaceful. The chief minister offered talks.
